This is incorrect, because in the NFL that isnt all guaranteed money. Contracts are often structured so that the team can cut a player at little or no cost if they arent performing and players often sign big long term free agent contracts but only ever see a.fraction of it because they get hurt, or start to suck, or whatever and the team cuts them. Then they can go get a contract with someone else.

For example, a player will sign something like a 5 year $55 million contract that is structured with $10 mil each the first three years and 12.5 mil each of the last two. They have $5 mil guaranteed each of the first 3 seasons and $1 mill each of the last two. The marginal cost to keep that player for seasons 1-3 is only $5 mil because they must pay $5 of that if he's on the team or not. The last two the marginal cost is 11.5 mil each season so if he isnt playing up to that kind of money it's very likely he'll be cut or will renegotiate so he can stay on the team.
